_what: How an account is deleted completely when its person asks (src/account/erase.rs, the port of old trillion src/account-erasure-policy.mjs with its pace, src/account-deletion-pace.json and records/native-lifecycle-continuation.json). `row_prefix` starts the id of the one kept deletion row in the account's own lists (src/account/rows; the account's user id follows). `steps` is the order the steps run in, each erasing one owner's rows through that owner's own functions (old continueAccountErasure: tool runs first, the account's store after, its own rows last); every step is one of `tool-runs`, `files`, `records`, `account-rows`, and `account-rows` is last, since it removes the account's computers rows, which say where the account is answered. One call takes at most `pages_per_call` pages; each page is at most `rows_per_page` rows (or files, or runs as the step's owner bounds it). `records` are the record store resources of the account's own records the records step erases (src/storage/record_store_resources.json); its migration position and its resource identity are kept, so nothing is copied back into an erased account. A step that fails waits `failure_delays_ms[failures - 1]` (the last one past the end), and past `maximum_consecutive_failures` a step failing with the same words again waits `repeat_growth` times longer each time, up to `longest_repeat_delay_ms`; a failure its step says is passing (the store busy, a file held) waits `transient_delays_ms` instead and never counts. A page that moved nothing (no row erased, the same cursor) `stall_after` times in a row waits `repeat_growth` times longer each time, up to `longest_stall_delay_ms`. A step's kept failure words are cut to `shape_chars`.
